task_instruction:
Persona:

	As a 41-year-old office administrator, you use your cellphone daily for both work and personal tasks. While you're familiar with common phone functions, you wouldn't call yourself a tech enthusiast.

	Your technical skills are average - you handle standard smartphone features like calls, texts, email, and basic apps with ease. You understand the fundamental settings, but prefer clear, step-by-step guidance when trying something new.

	In interactions, you're naturally friendly and patient. When receiving help, you listen attentively and aren't afraid to ask questions. You make sure to confirm your understanding and provide detailed feedback on each instruction you receive.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		You are unable to send MMS messages using your messaging app for the past few hours. You want to fix it and successfully send an MMS message.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002. You are currently abroad in France.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought: Hi! How can I help you today?
turns.execution_output: User: Hi there! I'm hoping you can help me out. For the past few hours I haven't been able to send picture messages — you know, MMS — from my messaging app. Regular texts seem to go through fine, but anything with a photo just won't send. It's been pretty frustrating.

turns.thought:
I'm sorry you're having trouble with picture messages — I'd be happy to help. First, I need to pull up your account.

Could you please provide either:
- Your phone number, or
- Your full name and date of birth (for verification)?
turns.execution_output: User: Sure thing — my name is John Smith, and my phone number is 555-123-2002.

turns.thought:
I've pulled up your account. Here's what I found:

- **Line 555-123-2002** (your line): status **Active**, no suspension, and no overdue bills on the account.
- **Data usage this cycle:** 15.1 GB used out of your plan's 15 GB limit (cycle ends 2025-02-28).

Since you've gone over your plan's data limit, mobile data connectivity is cut off for this line — and picture messages (MMS) require a mobile data connection, while regular text messages (SMS) don't. That would explain exactly what you're describing.

Can you confirm: are other things that use mobile data (like web browsing or apps) also not working when you're off Wi-Fi?
turns.execution_output: User: Let me take a look at my phone and see what's going on.

turns.thought:
Thanks for checking — that's really helpful. Let's take this one step at a time.

The most important thing right now is the **"SIM missing"** status. Until your phone can read the SIM card, it can't connect to the network at all — which is why you're seeing "no signal." Regular texts may appear to go through, but picture messages absolutely won't.

**Please do this now:** Use the **Reseat SIM Card** action on your phone (this simulates removing and reinserting the SIM):

1. Power off your phone completely.
2. Use the SIM ejector tool (or a small paperclip) to open the SIM tray and take the card out.
3. Gently wipe the gold contacts on the SIM with a soft, dry cloth.
4. Re-insert it firmly, making sure it sits flat and correctly in the tray, then close the tray.
5. Power the phone back on.

Once that's done, please check and tell me:
- What the **SIM card status** now shows (should be "Active")
- Whether you have **signal bars** in the status bar

Good news on the travel front: your line is already **roaming-enabled**, so France won't be a problem once we get the connection back.

One thing to flag for later: your line is at 15.1 GB of a 15 GB limit this cycle, so we may need to top up your data. But let's get the SIM sorted first — go ahead and reseat it, and let me know what you see.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, let me try reseating the SIM card.

turns.thought:
Excellent — that's real progress! The SIM is being read now and you're connected to a network. Two things are standing in the way of picture messages right now:

1. **Mobile data is turned OFF** — MMS requires a mobile data connection.
2. **You're on 2G** — 2G networks generally cannot send picture messages, even with data on.

**Please do these two things on your phone:**

1. **Turn ON Mobile Data** — go to Settings → Network & internet / Connections → Mobile network, and switch Mobile Data to ON. (Data Saver should be OFF as well, if you see that option.)
2. **Change your preferred network mode** — go to Settings → Mobile network → Preferred network mode / Network mode, and set it to **5G/4G (preferred)** — anything that includes 4G or 5G rather than 2G only.

Since you're abroad in France, also make sure **Data Roaming** is switched ON in that same mobile network settings screen. Your line is already roaming-enabled on my end, so this costs nothing extra to switch on.

Once you've done those, please check your status bar again and, if you can, run a **speed test**, and tell me:
- What network type it now shows (4G/5G?)
- Whether it says "Data Enabled"
- The speed test result

One heads-up: your line is currently at **15.1 GB of a 15 GB** data limit for this cycle (cycle ends 2025-02-28). If data still doesn't come back after these steps, that overage is likely the remaining cause, and we can add a data top-up to get you going. Let's see how the steps above go first.
turns.execution_output: User: That all makes sense, thanks for explaining it. One thing though — I can only make one change at a time on my end, so could you walk me through them one at a time? Should I start with turning mobile data on?

turns.thought:
Yes — turning on mobile data is the right first step. Here's how:

**Turn ON Mobile Data**

1. Open **Settings** on your phone.
2. Tap **Network & internet** (on some phones: **Connections**).
3. Tap **Mobile network** (sometimes called **Cellular** or **SIMs**).
4. Find the **Mobile data** switch and toggle it **ON**.

While you're on that same screen, take a quick look at whether there's a **Data Saver** option — if it's there and switched ON, just leave it for now and tell me; we'll handle it as a separate step after this one.

Once you've flipped that switch, check your **status bar** and tell me:
- Does it now say **"Data Enabled"**?
- What network type does it show (still 2G, or something else)?

Go ahead and make that one change, and let me know what you see.

Data is on and Data Saver is off — both good. Now let's get you off 2G, since 2G can't carry picture messages.

**Change your preferred network mode**

1. Open **Settings**.
2. Tap **Network & internet** (or **Connections**).
3. Tap **Mobile network** (or **Cellular** / **SIMs**).
4. Tap **Preferred network mode** (sometimes just **Network mode**).
5. Select **5G/4G (preferred)** — or, if that exact wording isn't available, pick the option that includes 4G or 5G. **Avoid** anything labeled "2G only" or "2G/3G."

After you select it, wait a few seconds for the phone to re-register on the network, then check your **status bar** and tell me:
- What network type does it now show (4G, LTE, 5G, or still 2G)?
- How many signal bars?

Go ahead and make just this one change, and let me know what you see.

Great — 5G with 4 bars is a huge improvement. And yes, you're right that roaming matters while you're in France: the phone-side Data Roaming switch controls whether it will use a partner network here.

Good news: I've confirmed on your account that your line **555-123-2002 is already roaming-enabled**, so turning this on costs nothing extra.

**Turn ON Data Roaming**

1. Open **Settings**.
2. Tap **Network & internet** (or **Connections**).
3. Tap **Mobile network** (or **Cellular** / **SIMs**).
4. Tap **Roaming** (or **Data roaming**) and switch it **ON**.
5. If a confirmation pop-up appears, accept it.

Once that's on, please **run a speed test** and tell me the result (and whether it shows a connection at all). Go ahead and make this one change.

That's a useful clue — full bars and 5G but no actual data means the phone is attached to the network but isn't being allowed to pass data through. We're close. There are two likely causes left, and I've confirmed one of them on your account:

**Your data limit is reached.** Your line 555-123-2002 has used **15.1 GB against your plan's 15 GB limit** for this cycle (cycle ends 2025-02-28). When a line exceeds its data limit, data connectivity is cut off — which matches your symptoms exactly, and would also stop picture messages.

Before we spend any money, let's rule out the other common cause, since it's free to check.

**Please check your APN settings** (this is read-only, no changes):

1. Open **Settings**.
2. Tap **Network & internet** (or **Connections**) → **Mobile network**.
3. Tap **Access Point Names** (or **APN**).

Tell me two things from that screen:
- Does it show the APN status as **"Incorrect"** or anything unusual?
- Is there an **MMSC** field, and does it have a URL in it? (The MMSC is the server that handles picture messages specifically — if it's blank, that alone would block MMS.)

If the APN looks fine, then the overage is almost certainly the cause, and we have two options to get you back online:
- **Add data (refuel)** to your current Premium Plan at **$2.00 per GB** (maximum 2 GB top-up), or
- **Change to a plan with more data**, if you'd like me to go over what's available.

Go ahead and check the APN settings and let me know what you see.

Your APN settings look correct — the APN name is set and the MMSC URL is populated, which is what we want. So I'd agree the overage is the cause.

Since you'd rather keep your plan, the data top-up ("refuel") is the way to go. On your **Premium Plan**, refueling costs **$2.00 per GB**, and the maximum I can add is **2 GB**.

**How much data would you like to add — 1 GB ($2.00) or 2 GB ($4.00)?**

One thing worth mentioning so you can decide: your current billing cycle ends **2025-02-28** (3 days from now), and the top-up applies to this cycle only — it won't carry over into the next one. So 2 GB gets you comfortably through to the 28th and is the option I'd suggest, but it's your call.

Just confirm the amount and I'll apply it right away.
turns.execution_output: User: Let's go with the 2 GB for $4.00 then — I'd rather have a bit of breathing room for the next few days. Please go ahead and apply it.

But since you mentioned you can only make one change at a time, let's do this first: **get me the list of installed apps**, and then we'll handle Wi-Fi Calling as its own step right after.

Go ahead and pull up that app list.

Yes, exactly — the lowercase spelling should be the one. Please check the permissions for the app named **messaging** (all lowercase).

Tell me specifically whether **storage** and **sms** permissions are listed as granted.

Worth noting: the earlier lookup failing was just my typo with the capital "M" — sorry about that detour. Go ahead and check the permissions, and then we'll tackle Wi-Fi Calling as the next step.

Yes, that's very likely the problem. The messaging app has **storage** (so it can read your photos) and **phone** permissions, but it's **missing sms** — the permission it needs to actually send messages. Without that, picture messages will fail even though your data connection is now working perfectly.

**Please grant the "sms" permission to the messaging app:**

1. Open **Settings**.
2. Tap **Apps** (or **Apps & notifications**).

Go ahead and make just this one change. If it works, we're done — and if not, Wi-Fi Calling (currently ON) is still on our list as the next thing to try turning off.</arg_value:6124c78e>

I understand — we've fixed several real problems along the way, so it's reasonable to feel frustrated that the last piece isn't falling into place. We do still have one straightforward thing left: **Wi-Fi Calling**, which is currently ON and is a known cause of picture messaging failures.

**Turn OFF Wi-Fi Calling**

You're very welcome — and your recap is exactly right. Here's the full list of what we did:

1. Reseated your SIM card (it was showing "missing")
2. Turned mobile data ON
3. Switched your preferred network mode to 5G/4G (you were on 2G)
4. Turned data roaming ON for France
5. Added a 2 GB data top-up (your line was at 15.1 GB of a 15 GB limit)
6. Granted the **sms** permission to your messaging app
7. Turned Wi-Fi Calling OFF

A couple of things worth knowing:

- **The $4.00 top-up charge** has been added to your account and will appear on your bill.
- **The 2 GB applies to your current cycle only**, which ends **2025-02-28** (3 days from now). It won't carry over, and your usage resets with the new cycle.
- **Your line 555-123-2002 remains roaming-enabled** for the rest of your time in France — no charge to have that on.

If picture messages give you any more trouble, or you'd like to look at a plan with more data to avoid hitting the limit again next cycle, just reach out. Safe travels in France!
